source_review.notes: Checked current Linux path-resolution, inode, ACL, access, chmod, chown, capabilities, xattr, and mount man-pages plus current Linux kernel idmapping documentation. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; generic authorization models, POSIX ACL rules, Linux-specific interfaces, illustrative execution, remote-policy guidance, and assurance remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked credential C with real, effective and filesystem IDs, supplementary groups, capabilities, user namespace and label; object O with identity, type, owner, group, mode, ACL, xattrs, flags and label; mount M; request A; permission subsets; ACL intersection; and authorization composition.
Reviewed DAC, credential snapshot, directory search, access and default ACL, ACL mask, capability, idmapped mount, mount flags, set-ID, sticky, mandatory policy, and delegation terminology.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates subject, stable object and parent, pathname context, identity mappings, DAC branch, additional policy, operation, and time.

evidence: Executed the illustrative ACL model and confirmed stored entry rwx intersected with mask r-x yields effective r-x.
Confirmed effective read and execute requests return true while write returns false.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic model demonstrates only set intersection; it excludes ACL branch selection, identities, groups, paths, capabilities, mounts, mandatory policy, races, and real kernel behavior.

evidence: Re-derived ACL order as mapped owner, exact named user, matching group class, then other, with the mask applied to named-user and group-class results but not owner or other.
Checked Allow(A) as the required composition of search, operation DAC or scoped override, mount and inode constraints, capability scope, mandatory policy, and current stable object state.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter does not infer permission from pathname text, union all mode classes, compare unmapped raw IDs, or equate DAC grant with total authorization.

evidence: Reviewed real, effective, filesystem, group and mapped IDs; owner, named user, multiple matching groups, other and masks; files, directories, symlinks, devices; read, write, execute, search, create, delete, rename, link, chmod, chown, xattr and descriptor use.

Reviewed umask and default ACL, setuid and setgid, sticky directories, file capabilities, user namespaces, idmapped mounts, read-only, noexec, nosuid and nodev mounts, immutable and append flags, mandatory policy, check-use races, descriptor passing, remote caches, malformed ACLs, unmappable IDs, and crashes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Identity, path, object, operation, inheritance, privilege, mount, namespace, policy, concurrency, distributed, recovery, and adversarial boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced context capture, safe resolution, identity binding, exact DAC evaluation, additional policy, actual mutation, privilege-state preservation, recoverable publication, retained authority, closed failure, composed testing, and evidence through twelve obligations, ten examples, and five answers.
Verified decision-use identity, per-directory search, ACL masking, atomic creation derivation, set-ID and capability clearing, handle stability, and policy-aware audit.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter does not conflate directory read with search, target write with unlink authority, chmod with descriptor revocation, noexec with full sandboxing, xattrs with inert data, or local DAC with remote authorization.

evidence: Reviewed credential consistency, per-component traversal, parent and target identity, DAC selection, override scope, metadata transition, descriptor semantics, revocation, remote caching, recovery, and evidence obligations.

Constructed counterexamples for pathname authorization, owner-plus-group union, ignored ACL mask, permissive-create-then-chmod, access-then-open, raw UID comparison, retained capability after overwrite, target-write unlink, noexec-only sandbox, and stale remote ACL cache.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable authorization proof obligations, not a formal proof of POSIX, Linux VFS, an LSM, filesystem, container runtime, identity service, or remote server.

evidence: Audited uses of owner, effective, permitted, denied, privileged, authoritative, stable, mapped, inherited, revoked, secure, durable, and certified.
Confirmed POSIX ACL semantics, Linux-specific interfaces, generic abstractions, illustrative execution, empirical tests, remote guidance, and assurance remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: UID zero is not presented as universal override, access as safe preflight, chmod as handle revocation, file capability as ordinary xattr, mount flags as complete sandbox, or a mode-bit matrix as certification.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-048/report.json records source, stored entry, mask, effective permissions, read, write and execute requests, stdout, stderr, and Python version.

Reviewed required collection of stable identities, mapped credentials, ACL branch and mask, capability, mounts, inode constraints, policy generation, operations, errors, races, remote state, audit output, raw traces, and limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes only ACL mask arithmetic; it provides no evidence for kernel path resolution, DAC, capabilities, namespaces, mandatory policy, remote authorization, or durability.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed subjects, objects, operation rights, path search, directory semantics, file read, write and execute, mode classes, creation masks, default and access ACLs, mask and evaluation order, chmod, ownership, set-ID, sticky directories, file and process capabilities, user namespaces, idmapped mounts, mount and inode controls, xattrs, mandatory policy, access and open, handle authority, descriptor passing, namespace mutations, links, remote caches, workflows, audit, testing, security, and assurance as coupled concepts.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed Linux fsuid and groups, per-component search, owner and group selection, ACL masks and inheritance, umask, sticky and setgid directories, set-ID and file-capability clearing, CAP_DAC overrides, user-namespace scope, idmapped ownership, mount flags, immutable state, access versus faccessat2, descriptor-relative opening, protected links, xattr namespaces, and remote mapping as implementable concerns. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from contextual authorization and path search through DAC and ACL mechanics, creation and privilege transitions, namespaces and layered policy, then race-resistant APIs, remote behavior, audit, testing, and assurance, followed by twelve trade-offs, fourteen misconceptions, ten examples, and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, POSIX authority, Linux VFS, ACL, capability, namespace or filesystem maintainer, LSM, container, identity, remote-storage, concurrency, audit, recovery, independent-verification, or certification review is claimed.
